cards.text: Isaiah the prophet is passing along words from the LORD, and now the LORD speaks about Assyria. It opens with "Woe to Assyria" right out of the gate. Friend, when a message opens with woe, you do NOT want your name right after it.

cards.question: The LORD calls Assyria "the rod of My anger" in this message. What does that make Assyria?

answers.text: The tool God uses to show His anger
The nation God trusts the most
The land God promised to protect

cards.text: Then God says He'll send Assyria out on a mission. Take spoils, seize plunder and trample them down like clay in the streets.

cards.question: True or false: God sends Assyria against a nation that has been faithful to Him.

cards.text: That's the job. But the LORD says this is not Assyria's intention, this is not his plan.

cards.question: God sends Assyria on His mission, but Assyria has a plan of his own. What's in his heart?

answers.text: To destroy and cut off many nations
To make peace with every nation
To bring the people back to God

cards.text: Then Assyria starts bragging: "Are not all my commanders kings?" Friend, I run six stations and I just go by Papa, and this guy's MIDDLE MANAGERS are kings?
Then he pairs up cities: Calno like Carchemish, Hamath like Arpad, and "Is not Samaria like Damascus?" Friend, this man is reading his own highlight reel out loud.

cards.question: True or false: When Assyria lists those cities, his point is that Samaria will be harder to take than Damascus.

cards.text: He says his hand has already seized other kingdoms. Then he sizes them up next to Samaria and one more city.

cards.question: Assyria compares the kingdoms he seized with Samaria and one more city. What does he say those kingdoms had more of?
Assyria says he's already done it to Samaria and its idols. So he asks: will I not also do it to ___ and her idols?

cards.text: Now the Lord has His say. When He has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He speaks about the king of Assyria, the one doing all that bragging.

cards.question: Once His work against Jerusalem is done, the Lord will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his ___ heart.
The Lord says He'll punish the king for the things he says about his victories. True or false: The king of Assyria gives the LORD the credit for them.

cards.text: The king says, "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever." Friend, nobody clever has EVER said "for I am clever" out loud.
He keeps going: he's removed the boundaries of nations, plundered their treasures and subdued their rulers. He says it was like reaching into a nest and gathering abandoned eggs.

cards.question: The king says that as he gathered the earth, no wing fluttered and no beak opened or chirped. What's he bragging about?

answers.text: Nobody even tried to stop him
He struck while the world slept

cards.text: Then comes the answer to all that bragging, and it's a question: "Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?"

cards.question: True or false: In that picture of the axe, Assyria is the axe and the LORD is the one swinging it.

cards.text: "Does a saw boast over him who saws with it?" Friend, I'm a stamper, and I never once stamped a cookie and turned around to Mother Miller like, "You're WELCOME," or I'd have landed in that drawer a whole lot sooner.
So the Lord GOD of Hosts will send a wasting disease among Assyria's stout warriors. And under all that pomp, He's got something else coming too.

cards.question: God is the Light of Israel and its Holy One. For Assyria, that Light will become a ___.

cards.text: That fire kindled under all his pomp comes for Assyria's thorns and thistles. Then the splendor of its forests and orchards goes too, both soul and body, as a sickness consumes a man.

cards.question: True or false: The fire takes years to burn through Assyria's thorns and thistles.
When the fire is done, how many trees are left in Assyria's forests?

answers.text: So few a child could count them
Just enough to build one house
One left standing on each hill

findings.problem: Assyria appears for the first time with no short line saying what it is, such as a nation or empire. The card introduces Isaiah but not Assyria.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card leaves out who Assyria is sent against so card 4 can ask about it. That leaves 'trample them down' with no one for 'them' to refer to, so the moment doesn't make sense on its own. The card also has almost none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question asks what those kingdoms 'had more of.' Isaiah 10:10 says their images 'surpassed' those of Jerusalem and Samaria, which doesn't specify number. 'More of' narrows the text. Card 10 also gives no context pointing to images or idols, so the answer comes down to luck.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The setup calls the king 'the one doing all that bragging.' That rules out 'humble' and 'fearful' in card 2 before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'nobody clever has EVER said "for I am clever" out loud' laughs at the king and his intelligence. It isn't self-deprecating, and it doesn't laugh with his human situation.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He struck while the world slept' can be argued from the image in Isaiah 10:14. Birds that don't flutter or chirp could be asleep, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke names Mother Miller without saying who she is. Nothing earlier in this lesson sets her up, and the docs only say bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding. A stranger would ask who she is.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.
